requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
I judge that the sources satisfy `requirements.ci.span`. The implementation covers each obligation and is marked `{impl}`. The tests cover the main cases. I found one minor point to note and no acknowledged gaps (no FIXMEs).

**Implementation**
- `src/lib.rs` `colon_fence` (marked `{impl}`) accepts a line only if it has at most three leading spaces and at least three colons. Four or more spaces of indent means it is not a fence.
- `src/lib.rs` `definition_blocks` (marked `{impl}`) handles the opening fence. It requires `{req}` right after the colons, then whitespace, then a valid name (`valid_name`).
- It finds the closing fence as the first line after the opening that is a colon fence with `count >= fence_length` and nothing but whitespace after the colons. A line such as `:::foo` therefore does not close the block.
- Lines inside CommonMark code blocks are skipped via `overlaps_protected`. This keeps a `:::` inside a fenced example or diagram in the body. It also makes the body "all Markdown between those fence lines".
- The body runs from the line after the opening fence to the start of the closing-fence line (`body_start..body_end`), so text after the closing fence is excluded. An unclosed block runs to end of file and is reported as an error by `collect_definitions`.
- `src/evidence.rs` `collect_definitions` has an `{impl}` comment at the body extraction. It takes the body between the fence lines, strips option lines, and applies `.trim()`. This excludes leading and trailing whitespace from the definition text, which is then compared with the evidence text in `validate_evidence_file` (covered by `requirements.ci.requirement_text`).

**Tests** (all marked `{test}`)
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` covers a body with a code block containing `:::` and `# heading`, ATX and setext headings, and text after the closing fence. It also covers a second requirement.
- `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` covers whitespace trimming.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` covers a longer outer fence containing a nested `:::` directive.
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` covers the closing-fence text rule and 3-space versus 4-space indentation for both opening and closing fences. It also covers a missing space after `{req}` and an unclosed block.
- `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` and `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` cover the end-to-end behaviour.

**Minor points**
- The whitespace trim is applied to the declaration body. Evidence text is compared exactly against it. This matches the wording "excluded when comparing the body".
- `overlaps_protected` is marked only with `markdown_literals`, but it is used inside the marked `definition_blocks`, so the behaviour is covered by a marked function.
